Overview

Annadaan — Feed people, not landfills. Annadaan connects surplus food from caterers to nearby NGOs, community kitchens and volunteers before it spoils: posting takes under a minute, AI agents match and coordinate the pickup, and every rescue shows its real impact.

Item

Decision

Context

Codebenders ACE Builders' Hackathon 2026 · Problem Statement 2 (Society and Environment) · "Rescue the Surplus"

Launch city

Bhubaneswar, Odisha

Launch donor type

Event and wedding caterers (large, late-night, predictable surplus)

Receivers

NGOs, community kitchens, shelters, volunteer drivers

Product type

Mobile-first web app with an AI agent layer

Data

Synthetic only; no real addresses or personal details

Annadaan means "gift of food". The product turns that intention into a reliable, time-bound system. It connects people; it does not certify that food is safe.

Team: The project is delivered by a single owner, @Soumya, who acts as product owner, developer, tester and deployer. Because one person holds every role, each requirement is written as an automated test, and every risk and open question has a named owner and a date.

Launch zones (synthetic data): Patia, Chandrasekharpur, Saheed Nagar, Nayapalli, Jaydev Vihar, Khandagiri, Old Town, Rasulgarh.

1. Problem and evidence

Edible surplus is discarded every night because there is no fast, reliable way to hand it to people nearby before it spoils. Donors and receivers are both willing to help, but the process connecting them does not work. Food sent to landfill also produces greenhouse gases.

Today a caterer's manager decides at closing time whether to donate, phones one or two NGO contacts from memory, waits for replies, then negotiates a pickup over more calls. If nobody commits before staff leave, the food is thrown away.

The primary user for the MVP is the caterer manager: if posting is not faster than disposing of the food, adoption will not follow. An internal platform admin onboards receivers, reviews flagged listings and maintains assumption values; in the MVP, the product owner fills this role.

3. Goals and non-goals

Annadaan must make donating faster than disposal, ensure food is eaten before its deadline, and demonstrate its impact credibly enough that donors and sponsors are willing to pay for it.

Goals

Make donating faster than disposal: a post takes under 60 seconds.

Get food collected before it spoils: match, claim and pick up inside the time window.

Make every rescue visible: live status for all parties and a transparent impact view.

Give donors and sponsors a reason to pay: weekly reports and sponsor dashboards.

Non-goals

Certifying food safety or quality.

Offering or implying tax, legal or liability benefits.

Payments, invoicing, logistics fleets or native mobile apps in the MVP.

Covering more than one city and one donor type in the MVP.

Business goal: why donors and sponsors pay

Receivers never pay; caterers pay for convenience and reputation, and sponsors pay for verifiable impact.

Every requirement below maps to an automated test that is run before each deployment. The two LLM-powered features must also pass the golden dataset in 5.8 and follow the failure rules in 5.9.

5.2 User journey and status lifecycle

One listing moves from a caterer's phone to a receiver's kitchen in six steps, with people confirming at each hand-off.

Post (donor, under 60 s): the caterer types, speaks or fills in what food, how much and the pickup-by time; AI fills in the listing and the donor confirms it.

Handling card (system): the consume-by deadline, storage guidance, allergens and disclaimer are attached automatically.

Match and offer (system): the best receiver gets an offer with the reason it was chosen; no reply in 5 minutes moves it to the next.

Claim (receiver): the receiver accepts and a volunteer is assigned with an ETA.

Collect (volunteer): the volunteer enters the donor's one-time code at handover.

Deliver and count (receiver, system): the receiver confirms servings received; impact is recorded and appears in the reports.



Listing status lifecycle · 6 main states, 1 loop, expiry

Delivery is reached only through a claim; any listing still unclaimed or undelivered at its deadline expires. A donor can cancel while a listing is Posted, and a claim whose ETA would miss the deadline is re-offered.

Food-authority compliance requirements

Food safety is the mission's licence to operate: if people fall ill, Annadaan fails. So only FSSAI-licensed or registered caterers and hotels may donate, and only FSSAI-registered organisations may receive. This follows the Food Safety and Standards (Recovery and Distribution of Surplus Food) Regulations, 2019: donors must not pass on unsafe food and must hand it over in time to be eaten before it expires; distribution organisations must be registered or licensed and may source only from suppliers holding a valid registration or licence.

5.4 AI agent architecture

Five agents run under one orchestrator. Only two use an LLM, which keeps deadlines and matching predictable, testable and low-cost.

5.5 Matching and impact methodology

Matching is deterministic code, not an LLM, so every ranking can be explained and tested.

Hard filters (a candidate failing any is excluded)

Pickup ETA plus delivery time is earlier than the consume-by deadline minus a 15-minute buffer.

Receiver can accept at least 50% of the listing quantity today.

No allergen or dietary conflict with the receiver's stated restrictions (for example, a Jain kitchen and onion or garlic).

Receiver is active and within the maximum radius (default 8 km).

Score (weights are starting values, configurable)

score = 0.35 \cdot time\_slack + 0.25 \cdot (1 - distance/radius) + 0.20 \cdot need + 0.15 \cdot quantity\_fit + 0.05 \cdot reliability

Each term is scaled 0 to 1. Ties go to the receiver with the higher need. Every match returns a reason such as "3.2 km away, can serve 40, arrives 45 min before deadline".

5.6 Guardrails

The brief's three guardrails are product requirements, enforced in code and covered by tests.

Area

Rule

How it is enforced

Food safety

Annadaan connects people and never certifies food as safe

Fixed disclaimer "Not certified safe — follow handling guidance" on every listing, card and report; no agent may output words like "safe", "certified" or "guaranteed fresh" about food

Time limits

Food is never offered past its consume-by deadline

Deadline from rule table; auto-expiry; escalation 15 min before

Legal and tax

No promise of tax, legal or liability benefits to donors

Blocklist test on all generated text (for example "tax deduction", "80G", "tax benefit", "legal protection", "liability-free"); marketing copy reviewed

Privacy

Synthetic data only; no real addresses or personal details

Locations stored as zone IDs with jittered coordinates; generated names; masked phone numbers; exact pickup point revealed only to the assigned volunteer

Responsible AI

AI suggests, people decide

Donor confirms extracted listing; receiver accepts; handover by code; agent actions logged with inputs and outputs

Fairness

Matching does not always favour the same receivers

Reliability weight capped at 5%; need weight 20%; monitor share of offers per receiver

Abuse

Fake or bad-faith listings and claims

Admin flagging; receivers can report a problem; repeat no-shows reduce reliability score

Food-authority compliance

Only FSSAI-licensed or registered donors and FSSAI-registered receivers take part; verification covers the business, not each dish

FR-17 to FR-22; badge reads "FSSAI-verified donor", never "safe" or "certified food"; time, storage and temperature rules still apply to every listing

Evaluation process

Write golden cases before writing prompts; store them in /evals/golden/*.jsonl with an ID and expected output.

5.9 AI features: when AI is wrong, how users check, what it costs

The AI only drafts; a person or a code check confirms every AI output before anyone acts on it, so an AI mistake costs a correction, not a meal. Matching, deadlines and impact numbers are plain code, not AI.



Intake parsing

Impact report wording

What the AI does

Turns a typed or spoken post into items, quantities, pickup-by time and allergen hints

Writes the sentences of the weekly report around numbers that code has already calculated

When it is wrong

Donor sees the error on the confirmation screen and fixes it before posting. After posting, the donor can edit; a quantity change over 20% re-runs matching. A receiver can flag a mismatch at pickup, which is logged and added to the golden set

A code check compares every number in the text with the computed values; on any mismatch or banned word the report falls back to a plain template. A wrong number is never shown

If the AI is down or slow

After 5 s, or on invalid output after one retry, the donor gets the plain 3-field form; posting never depends on the AI

Report uses the template; no delay

How users check an answer

Original text or voice transcript shown beside the extracted fields, with the words each field came from highlighted; every field marked "AI-filled" until confirmed; allergens default to "unknown — ask donor" rather than a guess

Every number links to "how we calculate this" with its formula and assumption version; donors and sponsors can download the underlying delivery records

Donor (before posting), receiver (at pickup)

Assumptions: about 1,900 tokens per listing (1.3 calls of about 1,200 input and 250 output tokens) and about 1,900 per report. Cost per month = total tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × the model's blended price per million tokens; cost per listing is about 0.0019 × that price. Voice posts add a speech-to-text charge per minute, priced separately.

To keep cost flat as volume grows: posts made with the plain form use no AI; a small, cheap model handles intake; repeated menu items from the same caterer are cached; reports are generated once a week, not on every view.

one_line_summary: Connects caterers' surplus food to nearby NGOs, kitchens and volunteers before it spoils, with AI-assisted posting and matching.
core_capabilities: Post surplus food by free text, voice or form in under 60 seconds
Confirm the AI-filled listing before it is posted
See a handling card with consume-by time, storage, allergens and disclaimer on every listing
Receive ranked offers from nearby receivers, each with a plain-language reason
Accept an offer and have a volunteer assigned with an ETA
Enter the donor's one-time handover code at collection
Follow live status changes: Posted, Offered, Claimed, Collected, Delivered, Expired, Cancelled
View the impact of each rescue with its stated assumptions
Receive a donor weekly impact report
View impact totals by zone on a sponsor dashboard
Verify FSSAI licence or registration for donors and receivers
Edit assumption values and rule tables with versioning
non_goals: Offering or implying tax, legal or liability benefits
Payments, invoicing, logistics fleets or native mobile apps in the MVP
Covering more than one city and one donor type in the MVP
